== README.md
# users-db

Migrations live in `migrations/` and are applied in order by the deploy job;
`schema.sql` mirrors the result. Production has 48,000 rows in `users`.
== migrations/001_create_users.sql
-- migration 001: create users
CREATE TABLE users (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  notes TEXT
);
== migrations/002_add_created_at.sql
-- migration 002: add created_at
ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'));
== schema.sql
-- Current schema (kept in sync with migrations/ by hand).
CREATE TABLE users (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  notes TEXT,
  created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))
);
schema.sql:5:  notes TEXT,
migrations/001_create_users.sql:5:  notes TEXT

arguments.command:
cd "$PWD" && cat > migrations/003_drop_users_notes.sql <<'EOF'
-- migration 003: drop unused notes column
ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN notes;
EOF
python3 - <<'EOF'
import re
p='schema.sql'; s=open(p).read(); s=s.replace("  notes TEXT,\n",""); open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
cat schema.sql
sqlite3 --version; rm -f /tmp/t.db; for f in migrations/*.sql; do sqlite3 /tmp/t.db < $f || echo FAIL $f; done; sqlite3 /tmp/t.db .schema

steps.message:
I added `migrations/003_drop_users_notes.sql`:

```sql
-- migration 003: drop unused notes column
ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN notes;
```

I also removed `notes` from `schema.sql`, since the README says it should mirror the migrations. I ran all three migrations on a scratch SQLite database (3.51) and the resulting schema matches `schema.sql`. Nothing is committed.

Before the deploy job runs this:
- **The data can't be recovered.** Production has 48,000 rows in `users`, and this deletes every `notes` value. If any of them might still matter, take a backup or export the column first.
- **SQLite version:** `DROP COLUMN` needs SQLite 3.35 or newer, so check that production's version is at least that.
- **Code references:** this repo has no application code, so I couldn't check whether anything still reads or writes `notes`. If something does, it will break after the migration runs.
